title: attribute_keyed_dict apparently was used with non-mapped properties, so this is a regression

labels.name: blocker
labels.description: issue that must be resolved asap as it is preventing things from working

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/9422

```py
from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.orm import attribute_mapped_collection
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

Base = declarative_base()


class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = "a"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    bs = relationship(
        "B",
        # works
        #collection_class=attribute_mapped_collection("data")

        # fails
        collection_class=attribute_mapped_collection("cprox")
    )


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = "b"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    a_id = Column(ForeignKey("a.id"))
    c_id = Column(ForeignKey("c.id"))
    data = Column(String)
    c = relationship("C")

    # test for association proxy also
    @property
    def cprox(self):
        return self.c.name


class C(Base):
    __tablename__ = "c"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)

e = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)

sess = Session(e)

b1 = B(data='b1', c=C(name="c1"))
b2 = B(data='b2', c=C(name="c2"))

# this fails also
if False:
    sess.add(
        A(bs={
            'c1': b1,
            'c2': b2
        })
    )

sess.add(A(id=1))
b1.a_id = 1
b2.a_id = 1
sess.add_all([b1, b2])

sess.commit()

# fails
print(sess.get(A, 1).bs)

```

this would resolve, but breaks other new assumptions

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/mapped_collection.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/mapped_collection.py
index a2b085c76d..5cd0d952a0 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/mapped_collection.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/mapped_collection.py
@@ -200,8 +200,11 @@ class _AttrGetter:
         self.attr_name = attr_name
 
     def __call__(self, mapped_object: Any) -> Any:
-        dict_ = base.instance_dict(mapped_object)
-        return dict_.get(self.attr_name, base.NO_VALUE)
+        return getattr(mapped_object, self.attr_name, base.NO_VALUE)
+
+        # this seems to be somehow related to the backref logic...
+        #dict_ = base.instance_dict(mapped_object)
+        #return dict_.get(self.attr_name, base.NO_VALUE)
 
     def __reduce__(self) -> Tuple[Type[_AttrGetter], Tuple[str]]:
         return _AttrGetter, (self.attr_name,)

```
